records.name: Arcadia Commons
records.summary: Neighbors who look after three green spaces in East Kensington so people have places to gather: Kern Park, The Huntingdon Emerald and the Emerald Wildflower Garden.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to water Kern Park or help tend its garden beds, join the mailing list, or give a donation. The group also runs free BBQs and workshops at its green spaces.

schedule.text: Volunteer shifts, such as watering Kern Park, are posted on sign-up sheets. The website lists no fixed weekly work days or times.

locations.label: Kern Park
locations.address: Kern Street, between E. Huntingdon and E. Sergeant Streets

locations.label: The Huntingdon Emerald and Emerald Wildflower Garden

cost.text: The website lists no fee for volunteering or joining, and it accepts donations.

first_step.how: Sign up for a watering shift at Kern Park through the group's sign-up link, or email info@arcadiacommons.us to ask about other volunteering.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page invites neighbors to take part and posts a sign-up link. It does not describe what a volunteer shift is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Watering Kern Park is the only task the volunteer page names. The site does not say how long a shift runs, what to bring, or whether children can help, so ask before you go. No fee is listed for volunteering.
first_visit_tips: Kern Park is on Kern Street between East Huntingdon and East Sergeant streets.
Ask the group what to bring, since the site lists no gear or age rules.
Confirm the shift time and place by phone or email, because the sign-up page did not show a readable sheet on this visit.

records.notes: Status changed from probably_active to dormant because the newest dated item on the news page is a post dated June 24, 2024, which is older than 24 months. The volunteer and sign-up pages carry no dates, so current activity is unconfirmed. The sign-up link opened a generic SignUpGenius page, not the Kern Park sheet. Before this shows as active, confirm with the group (phone or email) whether watering and other volunteer work is still running. Kern Park history dates (1912, 1913) are not evidence. Older 2017 news items mention Nature Heroes workshops and a Gardens for Good vote; they are not recorded as leads because no website was found.

records.name: Arch Street Friends Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Old City where people sit together in silent worship on Sunday mornings and on Wednesday evenings on Zoom. Families can use a children's program during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship in person, the Wednesday evening worship on Zoom, or the adult education series on fourth Sundays. Greeters welcome newcomers on Sundays, and refreshments follow worship. Ask the office how to get involved in committee and outreach work.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:30 am at the meetinghouse. Wednesday worship from 5:30 to 6:30 pm on Zoom. A children's meeting runs on the first to third Sundays from September to June, 10:30 to 11:15 am.

cost.text: No dues or fees are stated. The children's program and childcare are free.

access.notes: The entrance and restroom are wheelchair accessible, and a hearing loop is available. The children's room is on the second floor, and the pages read do not mention an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, where a greeter will meet you. Children from Pre-K through 8th grade can join the Children's Meeting on the first to third Sundays.
first_step.basis: The site has a Newcomer Resources page, greeters meet visitors on Sundays, and visitors are invited to attend. It has no orientation or first-timers event on the pages read.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship lasts an hour, from 10:30 to 11:30 am, and it is held in silence with no leader or planned program, though someone may speak. A greeter meets you, the hour ends with a handshake, and a social time with refreshments follows. On the first to third Sundays, children can join the free Children's Meeting, and younger children can use free childcare during worship.
first_visit_tips: Free, limited parking is on site during worship. The lot entrance is on 4th Street, halfway down the block from Arch Street.
Check septa.org for current transit routes, since the pages do not name a stop.
The website suggests watching an introductory video about Quakerism before a first visit.
The Wednesday Zoom link is in the weekly bulletin and the calendar, not on the pages read.

records.notes: Tier 1 said Sunday worship was also held on Zoom. The worship page does not mention Zoom at all, so Sunday Zoom is left out of the schedule text; the Wednesday Zoom session is on the home page. Pages give dates with no year (for example an October 11 children's meeting and worship, and an October 12 memorial meeting), so no dated evidence was recorded and status stays probably_active. Children's Meeting ages (Pre-K to 8th grade) come from its own page. Adult education runs on fourth Sundays September to June, with no sign-up described. Wheelchair rating is partial because the children's room is upstairs and no elevator is mentioned.

records.name: Arlen Specter US Squash Center
records.summary: A squash center that runs junior programs, a summer squash camp for players of every skill level, lessons, and club events.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can join junior programs, lessons, and the summer squash camp, and adults can take lessons too. You can book a court online. The site also lists memberships and venue rentals, and it does not list volunteer coach or mentor roles.

schedule.text: Open every day. Weekday hours close at 8 or 9 pm (the site lists both), and weekends run 9 am to 5 pm. Junior programs and lessons are scheduled on the online calendar.

locations.label: Center on the Drexel campus, University City

cost.text: Prices for lessons, junior programs, and memberships are not published on the pages read. Summer camp is paid in full at sign-up to reserve a spot.

first_step.how: Browse the online calendar, choose a junior program, lesson, or adult class, and register online. Contact the team for help, especially if it is your first time.
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome, the summer camp takes beginners, and it invites first-timers to contact the team for help.
first_step.what_to_expect: Players are grouped by age and skill, from beginners up to competitive juniors. Summer camp runs 9 am to 3 pm for full days or 9 am to noon for half days, with lunch provided and optional care until 5 pm. Prices are not listed on the pages read, so ask before you book.
first_visit_tips: Plan on non-marking sneakers and eyewear; the center lists both among the items you can borrow or buy.
Summer camp drop-off can start at 8:30 am.
30th Street Station is about two blocks away, according to the visit page.
Metered street parking is nearby, and the visit page lists garages at 3440 Market Street and 3386 Chestnut Street.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: 30th Street Station (regional rail), about two blocks away, as named on the center's visit page.

records.notes: No street address is recorded. The center's own site does not publish one, and two public sources disagree: Wikipedia lists 3205 Lancaster Avenue, and the SquashSmarts West Philadelphia page (a program run from the center) gives 25 N. 33rd Street. Confirm before adding an address. The site gives two sets of weekday hours (close at 8 pm in one place, 9 pm in another), so the schedule text says so. Camp dates carry no year on the page, which also refers to 2025 to 2026 camps. Camp needs at least 4 paying players each week to run. US Squash, the national body whose mailing address is on the contact page, is not listed as a lead. The tennis_pickleball tag is the nearest racquet sport because no squash tag exists. Email addresses on the contact page are hidden and are not recorded.
